runs.text: The Telugu word Kapu means “farmer” or “
protector

”. The Kapu community has different groups such as Balija, Munnuru Kapu, Telaga, and Turpu Kapu. They are also called Naidu, which means leader. In the past, Kapus were mainly soldiers and farmers. They fought in wars and farmed during times of peace.

Today, most Kapu people live in the southern Indian states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Tamil Nadu. Kapu is one of the largest communities in India (about 18% in Andhra Pradesh) and is becoming more influential in politics.

They are the descendants of the Kaampu tribe, an Indo-Aryan tribe. Kapus are classified as a Forward caste by both the Central Government of India and the Government of Andhra Pradesh. They are, on average, considered economically and educationally ahead of other castes. As of 2023, they do not offer any caste-based quotas or reservations. Kapu have banded together to fight for their political rights in the caste system. They have also organized agricultural unions to protect their way of life. A significant number of Kapu have today diversified into industry, arts, and academia. They are also politically active, advocating for their rights and interests.

The Kapu people are deeply tied to their Hindu faith, agrarian lifestyle, village traditions, and a growing sense of social identity. While rooted in traditional worship and ancestral reverence, their spiritual life is evolving with changing times, incorporating broader movements and personal growth practices.
“The LORD is your
keeper
; the LORD is your shade on your right hand. The sun shall not strike you by day, nor the moon by night. The LORD
will keep

will keep

will keep

Psalm 121:5-8 (ESV)
Pray for the Kapu people to know and experience that God is
their protector
Pray that God will open their eyes to see the limits of the caste system and their inability to defend their own political rights, so that they may come to the Lord, the eternal King, in repentance.
Pray that God will break the chains of customs and traditions related to Hindu beliefs and lead them into the truth so they can enjoy the freedom God gives.
Pray that God will raise His people who will pray for the Kapu tribe, love them deeply, and serve them with the heart of Jesus.
